t.2.76.1: Bharata, endowed with wisdom, beheld that assembly, filled with throngs of noble men and well-ordered, like a night graced by the full moon.
t.2.76.2: As the noble ones then took their seats in due order, the assembly looked like a night lit by the full moon once the clouds have passed away.
t.2.76.3: Seeing all the king's subjects assembled together, the family priest, knower of dharma, spoke these gentle words to Bharata.
t.2.76.4: Dear child, King Daśaratha, who lived by dharma, has gone to heaven after bestowing on you this prosperous earth, rich in wealth and grain.
t.2.76.5: Even so Rāma, steadfast in truth, ever mindful of the dharma of the virtuous, did not forsake his father's command, just as the risen moon does not forsake its radiance.
t.2.76.6: The kingdom, cleared of thorns, has been given to you by your father and by your brother. Enjoy it, with your ministers rejoicing, and have yourself consecrated without delay.
t.2.76.8: Having heard those words, Bharata, the knower of dharma, overwhelmed with grief, went in his mind to Rāma out of his longing for dharma.
t.2.76.7: Let the northerners, the westerners and the southerners, all of them, together with the peoples of the western borderlands and of the seacoasts, bring you jewels by the crore.
t.2.76.9: With a voice faltering and choked with tears, the young man, whose voice was like that of a kalahaṃsa swan, lamented in the midst of the assembly and reproached the family priest.
t.2.76.10: Who such as I would seize the kingdom of one who has practised the life of a celibate student, who has bathed on completing his learning, who is wise, and who ever strives in dharma?
t.2.76.11: How could one born of Daśaratha become a usurper of the kingdom? Both the kingdom and I belong to Rāma; you ought to speak here of what is dharma.
t.2.76.12: The eldest and the best, righteous of soul, the equal of Dilīpa and Nahuṣa, Kākutstha deserves to obtain the kingdom, just as Daśaratha did.
t.2.76.13: If I were to commit this sin, practiced only by the ignoble and barring the way to heaven, I would become in this world the disgrace of the Ikṣvāku lineage.
t.2.76.14: The sin that my mother has committed, I do not approve of it. Standing here with joined palms, I bow to him who dwells in the impassable forest.
t.2.76.15: I shall follow Rāma alone; he is the king, the best of men. Rāghava is worthy of the kingship even of all three worlds.
t.2.76.16: Hearing those words, imbued with dharma, all the members of the assembly, their hearts fixed upon Rāma, shed tears of joy.
t.2.76.17: But if I am not able to turn back the noble one from the forest, I shall dwell right there in the forest, just as the noble Lakṣmaṇa does.
t.2.76.18: I shall use every means to bring him back, even by force, in the presence of the noble elders and the virtuous men who live by good qualities.
t.2.76.19: Having spoken thus, the righteous-souled Bharata, devoted to his brother, then said this to Sumantra, skilled in counsel, who stood nearby.
t.2.76.20: Rise quickly and go, Sumantra, at my command; swiftly order the march and assemble the army.
t.2.76.21: Thus addressed by the great-souled Bharata, Sumantra, overjoyed, gave orders for everything just as he had been instructed, as if it were his own desire.
t.2.76.22: Those subjects, and the commanders of the army, rejoiced on hearing that the journey for the bringing back of Rāghava had been ordered.
t.2.76.23: Then, learning of the setting out on the expedition, all the wives of the warriors, delighted, urged on all their husbands in house after house.
t.2.76.25: Seeing that army made ready, Bharata, in the presence of his preceptor, said to Sumantra at his side, "Hasten my chariot!"
t.2.76.24: Together with the warriors, the commanders of the army urged on the entire host, with horses, swift ox-carts, and chariots fast as thought.
t.2.76.26: Accepting that command of Bharata, he, delighted, took a chariot yoked with the finest horses and set forth.
t.2.76.27: Then Bharata, that valiant Rāghava, steadfast in truth and firm and true in his prowess, spoke words most fitting, intending to win the favor of his illustrious elder who had gone to the great forest.
t.2.76.29: That son of a sūta, duly commanded by Bharata and with his wish wholly fulfilled, instructed all the chief men among the subjects, the leaders of the army, and the circle of friends.
t.2.76.28: Rise quickly, Sumantra, and go to the chiefs of the army for the mustering of the forces, for I wish to win the favour of Rāma, who dwells in the forest, and bring him back for the welfare of the world.
t.2.76.30: Then, rising up in every household, the warriors, the vaiśyas, the śūdras and the brāhmaṇas yoked camel-drawn chariots and donkeys, elephants and horses of noble breed.
